title: Build benchmark-driven harness improvement loop and deterministic skill verification
description:
Investigate and implement the parts of the autoagent methodology that fit homeclaw.

Context
- The useful part of autoagent is not its runtime harness. It is the benchmark-driven improvement loop: establish a baseline, change prompt/tools/orchestration, rerun evals, keep only improvements, and log every experiment.
- homeclaw already has a stronger runtime harness for household use: prompt and response rules, privacy enforcement, tool routing, skill creation/install/update, and background consolidation.
- The main gap is a lack of a scored, repeatable harness evaluation loop for real homeclaw behaviors.

Why this matters
- We need a disciplined way to improve response quality, tool use, skill creation, and determinism over time.
- Prompt growth alone is a weak improvement strategy. We need evidence-based changes backed by evals and tighter verification.
- The current system has several high-variance areas that should be made more deterministic, especially skill activation, skill verification, and tool-use validation.

Goals
- Build a repeatable eval loop for homeclaw behavior and harness changes.
- Make improvements measurable with baseline, rerun, and keep/discard criteria.
- Improve deterministic behavior around tool selection, side effects, privacy boundaries, and final responses.
- Add verification for generated or installed skills before treating them as production-ready.

Non-goals
- Do not import autoagent's single-file coding harness or coding-task assumptions.
- Do not run autonomous self-editing against production household data.
- Do not optimize for generic coding benchmarks; optimize for household assistant behavior.

Workstreams
1. Behavior eval corpus
- Create a deterministic eval suite for real homeclaw tasks using fixed household fixtures.
- Cover reply quality, tool selection, file side effects, privacy enforcement, memory writes, reminders, bookmarks, and routine behavior.
- Prefer deterministic assertions for correctness; use LLM-as-judge only for narrow style/tone checks.

2. Harness experiment loop
- Add a harness experiment runner that records baseline and variant results.
- Keep changes only when behavior improves, or stays equal while the implementation becomes simpler.
- Record experiment metadata and per-case outcomes for regression analysis.

3. Skill verification and certification
- Add a verification path for skill_create, skill_install, and skill_update.
- Verify parsing, loading, dependency availability, namespaced tool registration, sample scenarios, and data-file conventions.
- Distinguish between a skill that exists on disk and a skill that is verified for use.

4. Deterministic runtime improvements
- Reduce prompt-only behavior where repeated failures can be handled with explicit tools or validators.
- Replace LLM-generated activity-feed summaries with deterministic templates where possible.
- Make skill activation session-scoped instead of process-global.
- Tighten tool classification and routing based on eval evidence rather than intuition.

5. Response-quality controls
- Define measurable standards for concise replies, useful interim updates, and completion behavior after tool calls.
- Add regression cases for common bad patterns: empty acknowledgements, overlong responses, promising actions without tools, and weak follow-through after writes.

Acceptance criteria
- There is a committed eval corpus for core household assistant behaviors.
- There is a documented baseline/variant/keep-discard workflow for harness changes.
- Skill verification exists and is applied to create/install/update flows.
- At least one current nondeterministic runtime behavior is replaced with a deterministic implementation.
- Harness changes can be evaluated with a repeatable score or pass/fail report instead of ad hoc judgment.

Suggested child issues
- Build eval fixtures and scoring harness for core homeclaw behaviors.
- Add skill_verify and wire it into skill creation/install/update flows.
- Make skill activation session-scoped and deterministic.
- Replace LLM tool-feed summaries with deterministic summaries.
- Define and test response-style regression cases.
- Document the harness improvement workflow for contributors.

References
- autoagent repo: https://github.com/kevinrgu/autoagent/tree/main
- autoagent directive/program: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kevinrgu/autoagent/main/program.md
